title: Potato and Bramley rösti with fried eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, a Bramley, cornflour, butter, oil, eggs, Cheddar and garden thyme are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: A frying pan, grater and tea towel are all it needs, and grating, squeezing and frying cakes is well within a confident beginner's skills.

works.reason: The squeezed potato and apple bound with cornflour make four decent cakes, 6 to 8 minutes a side cooks them through, and the egg and Cheddar balance the sharp Bramley.

honest_times.reason: Grating and squeezing 600g of potatoes and an apple fits 15 minutes, and two sides of frying plus the eggs fits the 20 minutes of cooking for a reasonably quick breakfast.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the fresh thyme and the salt and pepper, is used in the steps, the names match their ids and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot, crisp potato and Bramley cake suits a cold December morning, and the apple is a named, substantial part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour could follow without fuss.

hearty_healthy.reason: Potato, apple, egg and cheese make a filling, real-food breakfast a family would happily eat again.
